newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing share market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing share market report.

text.p: Dutch shares climbed sharply on Tuesday to close at a record high, boosted by the continuing surge in the dollar, a fresh spate of encouraging Dutch company results and positive comments from Fed chairman Alan Greenspan on sustainable low-inflation U.S. growth.

"The dollar is very strong again today and therefore this market is doing extremely well," said one dealer. "Volume hasn't been that high...it's more a question that people don't want to sell when they think the market has higher to go."
The AEX closed 17.14 points, or 2.33 percent, up at a record 753.40, beating the previous 750.51 peak set on February 26.

"On top of the dollar rise we've had good results today from Hunter Douglas and Stork," he said, adding hopes were high that companies yet to report this week -- such as Ahold -- would continue the stream of good corporate news.
Dealers said the market could well be set to push back above the 755.73 AEX intra-day high, also reached on February 26. "The old high is very much within reach," said another dealer.

"With the market at these levels we're reaching a point when the options traders are beginning to buy in the cash market because they're betting on a lower AEX," he said. "If they leave it much longer they are going to get squeezed harder."
Some dealers sounded a warning against the speed of the AEX's advance which has seen over a dozen records fall during its 100-point plus rise from 648 since the end of last year.

"When you look at sentiment in this market it's extremely strong, but when you look at the valuation it's too high," said one dealer, adding that bullish sentiment could still prove stronger than a cold evaluation of underlying worth.

"My feeling is that sentiment is going to win out. We're going to see a new high in the short term," he said. Chart analysts are split on this week's direction in the AEX although most pencil in heavy resistance at the old high.

Window coverings maker Hunter Douglas closed 7.00 guilders higher at 153.00 after reporting a 26 percent rise in 1996 net profit to 158.3 million guilders, at the upper end of a 148 to 160 million guilder analysts' forecast range.
The shares were further boosted by news of a two for one stock split and a positive outlook for 1997.

Industrial systems group Stork closed 4.20 guilders firmer at 79.80, lifted by its announcement net profit rose to 137 million guilders in 1996 from 108 million the previous year. It too was positive about the future, predicting further profit growth in 1997.

Dealers said the scene was set for another batch of encouraging results on Thursday when Ahold, up 4.50 guilders to 129.80, Hoogovens, 2.90 higher at 91.30 guilders and BolsWessanen 1.10 guilders up at 34.60, report annual results.

Shares in Philips surged 4.20 guilders or 5.00 percent to a record high closing 89.90. Dealers said buyers had snapped up the stock on the prospect of 1997 growth as new chairman Cor Boonstra was seen successfully isolating loss making units.
Other dollar earners met demand with Royal Dutch up 6.40 guilders to 334.20 and Unilever 5.80 higher at 359.20 guilders. -- Keiron Henderson, Amsterdam Newsroom +31-20-504-5014
